Q: How to block CI/CD pipeline when npm HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerabilities are found? A:

You can use the DevShield CLI tool which handles all of this:

npx devshield

It audits your local package.json and automatically

blocks your CI/CD pipeline if HIGH or CRITICAL

vulnerabilities are found.

It also provides:

- CVE history and metadata for any npm package

- Maintenance signals (last publish, download stats)

- Risk scoring before you install

You can also check packages visually at devsheild.live

before adding them to your project.

Disclaimer: I'm the developer of this tool.

Q: How to learn SQL? A:

The key is to practice a lot.

First with basic queries then more and more and more complex ones.

Perhaps my method is a bit outdated but I usually like to read the documentation of the DBMS I’m working with. Then picking up examples from relevant chapters to practice them on my own.

Q: Is it a good or a bad idea to join two tables on several columns if joining on one column is enough? A:

In ClickHouse, joins gain benefit from sorted data only if one of the joined tables's storage order matches the join key. In your case, neither table's storage order is based on all three columns of the join key, so as I understand it, a sort-merge join is not possible.

I think it'll resort to a hash join, which ClickHouse treats as the default join algorithm. In this case, it doesn't matter that the tables are ordered, since it'll have to fill a hash table regardless.

There could always be edge cases depending on the size of tables, available memory, and so on. The best way to know for sure is to test both methods yourself using your data on your server.

Join algorithm selection in ClickHouse is complex, and I'm not an expert. I've only read a bit about it. If you're concerned with query optimization, I recommend reading the blog series on join types. It's a series starting here: https://clickhouse.com/blog/clickhouse-fully-supports-joins-part1

Q: Where in the C standard does it specify the corresponding argument for %n in fscanf shall be a pointer to int A:

Many of the other conversion specifiers state one of the following:

Unless a length modifier is specified, the corresponding argument shall be a pointer to int.

Unless a length modifier is specified, the corresponding argument shall be a pointer to unsigned int.

The fact that such as sentence is missing from the description of the n specifier is, as far as I can tell, a defect in the standard.

The statement in the standard about the n specifier

The corresponding argument shall be a pointer of a signed integer type.

is insufficient, because as correctly pointed out in the question, a long long int is also a "signed integer type".

Q: Should a DTO be generated by a domain entity or from persistence? A:

If I also have, say, an MVC web app I want to show a list of events on, I might want a view model that would look something like this

In async environment I don't think state matters, events in event_bus (that is in Infrastructure Layer in Clean Arch.) always can help to reconstruct any needed state. It seems, that is your goal - not ModelView, but model in microservice, communicating with any data-storage.

Look for Clean Architecture of Robert Martin: In Domain Layer you describe not only Entities (Model), but also some BL, domain events, domain services, interfaces, exceptions, enums...

Consider 1 domain to be 1 physical storage (e.g Docker container for deployment). If you transfer info to UI - generate DTOs in Application or Infrustructure Layers, using Domain just like DbContext (Entities), or now namely BoundedContext (in DDD).

If you transfer info between microservices (to another domain) - you still have some Infrustructure Layer inside each microservice (its own domain). And can define DTOs either in Application Layer or Infrastructere Layer.

Besides creating several smaller microservices in one larger microservice is also possible - all with their own layers.

If you don't want distributed development for distributed deployment (for scalability and maintainance) - you still can benefit from changing MVC architecture to Clean Architecture, because View layers are no more needed in modern projects if Views are stored separated in WebApps and you only asynchronously send info (with DTOs converted to JSON) to Views as a result of some events. In DDD I would prefer to define DTO in Application Layer, but use them from Infrastructure Layer. Though, of course, Domain Layer can also define DTOs (for simple CRUD oerations it is normal) - then just inject these dependencies wherever you like to use you API.

Just decouple Responsibilities between architectural Layers and physical storage correct and you will have no doubts where to create interface (as port), where to define its implementation (as adapter) and where and how to inject this Dependency into overall WebApplication (controller of which microservice will generate your json responces and requests converted from DTO).

Q: How can I get a hash of an entire table in postgresql? A:

We can build on the potent (undocumented) hash functions for records in modern Postgres. hash_record_extended(record, bigint) produces a bigint hash from a given row. (The second argument is a random seed; we can just use 0 there.)

About twice as fast as Weihang Jian's "fastest solution" in my tests:

SELECT sum(hash_record_extended(t, 0)) FROM tbl t;

Plus, bigint instead of integer, which makes hash collisions a whole lot less likely.

Related:

  • Why doesn't my UNIQUE constraint trigger?

Q: I've made a JWT service and I yet have to solve the authorization issue with my attendance controller in the Web API layer what's the solution? A:

It seems like that ASP.NET Core's JwtSecurityTokenHandler performs default mapping of certain JWT claims to ClaimTypes (e.g., sub, role, name).

I can answer your questions as follows:

  1. Add JwtSecurityTokenHandler.DefaultInboundClaimTypeMap.Clear(); to Program.cs

  2. Ensure the EmployeeId claim is present on jwt.io.

  3. Verify that the ValidateIssuer and ValidateAudience settings in your Program.cs match the strings used in the JwtService

Q: How to perform the "uncollapsing" of a one row data frame or array to multiple rows in R A:

Using base R, repeat the collapsed row producing a list and use list2DF to convert it to a data frame, d. Then fill in the upper triangle using NA.

d <- list2DF( lapply(collapsed, rep, length(collapsed)) )
result <- replace(d, row(d) < col(d), NA)

identical(result, uncollapsed)  # check
## [1] TRUE
